title: Certificates of Deposit: deciding whether an interest payout account has been closed
content:
## Scope

This rule applies to a Certificates of Deposit certificate whose Interest Disposition pays credited interest out to a PCB account rather than compounding it. It decides whether the payout account named for that interest has been closed.

## Rule

1. Only an Interest Disposition of **Pay to Checking** or **Pay to Savings** is concerned. Under a **Compound** Interest Disposition no payout account receives interest, and the question does not arise.
2. Whether the payout account has been closed is read from the status of the account named as the certificate's payout account, of the kind the Interest Disposition pays to:
   - for Pay to Checking, the status of that checking account;
   - for Pay to Savings, the status of that savings account.
3. A status of closed means the account has been closed.

## Input, judgement, output

| Interest Disposition | Account whose status is read | Status on the bank's record | Payout account closed? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pay to Checking | The named checking account | Closed | Yes |
| Pay to Checking | The named checking account | Active | No |
| Pay to Savings | The named savings account | Closed | Yes |
| Pay to Savings | The named savings account | Active | No |
| Compound | None | Not read | Not concerned |

## Points of judgement

**The Interest Disposition is Pay to Savings and the owner's checking account was closed last week. Is the payout account closed?**
No, not for this purpose: under Pay to Savings only the status of the named savings account is read.

**Who decides whether the account is closed, the owner or the record?**
The status on the bank's record of the named account.
